meaning: to be very clumsy when you use your hands
example: I can't fix anything in the kitchen because I'm all thumbs.
origin: The exact origin is unclear. It probably comes from the idea that thumbs make fine hand movements difficult when they are clumsy.

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal, physical description. The idiom is about how well you use your hands, not about your body.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be very good at fixing things
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite meaning. The idiom describes someone who is not skilled with their hands.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be able to count very quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with counting or numbers. It only describes clumsiness.

explanation: 'All thumbs' is an informal way to say that someone is clumsy and bad at tasks that need their hands. It is common when talking about abilities.
